title: Exchange Your Driving Licence in Spain: Test Rules and 6-Month Deadline
description: How to exchange a foreign driving licence in Spain: the 6-month deadline, which countries skip the test, the documents, typical costs and what to do if you miss it.
excerpt: UK licence holders can swap without a test. US licence holders cannot. Here is the deadline, the paperwork and the costs, before the clock runs out.
tldr: If you are a legal resident, you generally have 6 months to exchange a foreign licence. UK and some other countries can swap without a test for a small fee plus a medical certificate. US licence holders have no exchange agreement and usually need the full Spanish theory and practical tests.

segments.text: "Exchange UK driving licence Spain" and "how to exchange driving licence in Spain" are among the most searched questions by new residents, and the answer depends almost entirely on where your licence was issued and how long you have lived here. This guide covers the deadline, who can swap, what you need and what to do if you cannot.

Foreign residents are generally required to exchange or replace their licence within six months of starting legal residency. Guides differ slightly on exactly when the clock starts, with some pointing to municipal registration (empadronamiento) and others to the residence card, so the safe approach is to count from whichever comes first.

The stakes are real. Once the window closes, sources report that the simple exchange route can close and you may need to take the full Spanish tests. Driving on a foreign licence after the deadline can also cause problems with your insurance. If you are still sorting your paperwork, start with our

content.text: Which countries can swap without a test

segments.text: Spain has exchange agreements with a list of countries. Licences from EU and EEA states can be exchanged, and the United Kingdom is covered by a bilateral agreement that allows a test-free exchange. Published lists also include several Latin American countries, Japan and South Korea, among others.

The United States has no such agreement with Spain according to the guides we checked, so US licence holders generally have to pass the Spanish theory and practical tests, usually through a driving school. Because the agreement list is updated, always check the DGT's current list for your country before you plan.

content.text: What you need for a direct exchange

items: Passport and your NIE or residence card
A recent proof of registration (empadronamiento certificate)
Your original foreign licence, which is surrendered
A medical certificate from an approved driver assessment centre
The paid DGT fee receipt and the application form

segments.text: Costs quoted for 2026 are modest: a DGT fee of roughly €20 to €30 and a medical certificate of around €30 to €60, so about €65 to €100 in total for most people. You book the DGT appointment through the DGT online office, and guides report waits of a few weeks in big cities, so book early. You usually receive a temporary licence quickly and the permanent card by post later.

Start by confirming that your country is on the agreement list and noting your residency start date, because that sets your deadline. Next, get the medical certificate from an approved assessment centre, which is a short check of vision, hearing and reflexes, and keep it current, since it is only valid for a limited period. Then gather your registration certificate, photos and the paid fee receipt, and book the DGT appointment as early as you can.

At the appointment you hand over your foreign licence, which is surrendered, and receive a temporary Spanish licence while the permanent card is produced and posted to your registered address. Keep the temporary licence with you when driving, and update your address with the DGT if you move before the card arrives.

content.text: If you have to take the Spanish test

segments.text: If your country has no agreement, or you missed the deadline, you go through the normal licensing route: a theory test and a practical driving test, normally with an autoescuela. Published guides quote total costs of several hundred to a couple of thousand euros and timelines from a couple of months to longer, depending on your experience and how quickly you get test dates. Some driving schools offer English-language support or English-speaking instructors, which makes the theory part far easier.

content.lead: Driving schools with a checkable signal that they work in English, by area:

items: Book the DGT appointment as soon as you have your paperwork, because waits can be long
Do the medical certificate at an approved centre, not any clinic
Keep your foreign licence until you have your temporary Spanish one
Check with your insurer that you are covered while the exchange is in progress
If you are unsure which route applies to you, ask a driving school or the DGT before you spend money

segments.text: This is general information. Rules and agreement lists change, so confirm the current requirements with the DGT.

faqs.q: How long do I have to exchange my driving licence in Spain?
faqs.a: Generally six months from the start of legal residency. Count from registration or your residence card, whichever came first, and do not leave it to the last week.

faqs.q: Can I exchange a UK driving licence in Spain without a test?
faqs.a: Yes. UK licences can be exchanged under a bilateral agreement without a theory or practical test, provided you do it within the deadline and bring the right documents.

faqs.q: Can I exchange a US driving licence in Spain?
faqs.a: Guides report that there is no exchange agreement, so US licence holders usually need to pass the Spanish theory and practical tests. Check the DGT for the current position.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to exchange a licence in Spain?
faqs.a: Roughly €65 to €100 for most people: a DGT fee of about €20 to €30 plus a medical certificate of about €30 to €60.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the six-month deadline?
faqs.a: The simple exchange route can close and you may need to take the full Spanish tests. Driving on a foreign licence after the deadline can also affect your insurance.
